HRA Analysis: The two-year-old fillies come together in what looks a strong race. DANGER BEWARE (7) has been super impressive in both her runs so far and will again look to be storming home strongly from back in the field, where you would expect her to settle from the outside front-row draw. KOOKY (9) draws the back row for the first time, having led in all three starts since arriving back in the state. She follows out a handy beginner in IDEN JUST BECAUSE (2), who hasn't been far away in recent feature races against some of these fillies, so should find at worst a midfield position and get her chance to again be in the finish. ANN PENNY (8) is another who draws the back row for the first time since arriving from New Zealand but has shown good speed at both ends of her races thus far. With some tempo throughout and a good drive, you would expect her to be just as competitive coming from behind. BABY CHARLOTTE (5) got the gaps when needed last start at Burnie when a short-priced favourite and looks to be improving with every start. She was a handy second after doing all the work at her previous start, so will be looking to take advantage of her front-row draw ahead of her main dangers. VINJETTA (3) is still yet to break her maiden despite putting together some strong performances and again gets her chance from the nice draw, while SOUL OF KARALTA (6) could be the one at odds if she is able to utilise her sharp gate speed to find the pegs, as she did two starts back. Selections: DANGER BEWARE (7), KOOKY (9), BABY CHARLOTTE (5), ANN PENNY (8)

The first heat of the Dynamo Series kicks off, where there looks to be speed aplenty from some well-drawn runners. SOHO TIGER LILY (3) will be doing her best to get to the pegs, where she can run a very sharp mile when on song. However, WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2) and OUR WILLOW (1) also possess excellent gate speed, so the pressure could be on early, with all three racing very well and consistently of late. The beneficiary of that early speed could be KARALTA ARTEMIS (7), who has really hit his straps at his past three starts when driven with a sit and coming with one run late. In the smallish field, he should get his chance to do something similar here. ITSMENOTU (4) hasn't been far away in her two starts since resuming from a break and, although rising slightly in class, can't be left out of exotics. MR BONDI (6) looks the best of the rest and could be running home strongly off a solid tempo, with the mile distance suiting him where he does his best racing. Selections: KARALTA ARTEMIS (7), SOHO TIGERLILY (3), WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2), OUR WILLOW (1)

COLORADO GIRL (1) has been hit and miss since arriving in the state but looks to get her chance here from the pole draw over the short distance. Although she has been driven more quietly of late, she does possess very sharp gate speed from the mobile start, so expect connections may use that to their advantage here and attempt an all-the-way victory. Stablemate TWILIGHT BEACH (5) has hit the line well at her past two starts and will no doubt look to do something similar again from the middle front-row draw, where she should find a midfield position. STANTON BREAK (2) and GOBSMACKED (8) should position close to the speed with cover and get their chance over the final furlong. COOLANDCOLLECT 4) has been racing well without winning and only needs a good run in transit to be storming over the top of them late if at his best. Selections: COLORADO GIRL (1), TWILIGHT BEACH (3), COOLANDCOLLECT (4), GOBSMACKED (8)

The lowest-rated heat of the night looks to have gate speed aplenty off the front row, where CAPTAIN CHEDDAR (3), AWAY GAME (4) and FIVE STAR SHARK (5) all possess very good gate speed, and expect they will look to use it here. However, all three would need to improve on recent performances to be winning. DANCINWIVJOLENE (2) hasn't been far away of late and should get a nice soft run just behind the speed from her ideal draw. SWEET AMOUR (6) and NO NUKES SKIPPER (7) will be relying on that early tempo to allow them to run home strongly into the finish, where they could take some holding out late. Selections: DANCINWIVJOLENE (2), SWEET AMOUR (6), NO NUKES SKIPPER (7), FIVE STAR SHARK (5)

The highest-class heat of the night, where you would somewhat expect the fastest mile rate to come from. IMPERIAL LAZ (3) will be attempting to use his gate speed to get to the pegs in what looks a somewhat tricky speed map off the front row. At his best, he can run a very sharp mile and would be hard to run down. MUZZAME MATE (2) gets the nice draw and has sufficient gate speed to find a good position on speed. He deserves to break through after a string of strong performances. IDEN LADY LINCOLN (5) does her best racing on speed when driven tough, and expect connections may employ similar tactics here, which should ensure a strongly run race and allow every horse to get their chance. She will have to try to stave off the challengers late. ANGEL ROCKS (1) gets the pole draw to her advantage but would need to improve on her disappointing first-up effort. Selections: MUZZAME MATE (2), IDEN LADY LINCOLN (5), IMPERIAL LAZ (3), ANGEL ROCKS (1)

I found this race the hardest to assess of the night. THEE OLD BOMB (5) returns to the front row and can run the gate like no other when allowed. With no other standout gate speed horses off the front row, he should be first to the pegs and get his chance to run a sneaky race at odds. ALBERIO (6) also possesses good gate speed when asked and, although drawn wider, expect he should have enough speed to get across most of those inside him and hopefully find a nice position on speed. OLLIES MEDAL (8) would benefit from some good tempo throughout, which would allow him to settle better, and could be the knockout horse at odds as the lone backmarker. DOLCE DRAMA (7) is threatening to break through after some handy performances of late but draws the outside gate. DENNY (3) looks the most consistent of the other three Wayne Yole-trained pacers from their nice draws, in what looks a very difficult race where any runner could bob up and win. Selections: THEE OLD BOMB (5), ALBERIO (6), OLLIES MEDAL (8), DOLCE DRAMA (7)

STONE WRITER (1) returns to racing after a 12-month break and comes up with the pole draw on resumption. He trialled very nicely on Monday at Hobart and, if he puts his best foot forward, expect he may take some beating here. TALK IS CHEAP (5), you would expect, may have a crack for the front early using her good gate speed and is suited over the mile, as is COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2), who draws the ideal gate to find a nice position on speed. Another race where it wouldn't surprise to see any horse pop up and win, including EYE SEE AMOUR (6), who has been running home well of late, and the old girl QUEENOFDANCE (8), who loves sitting off the back of a hot tempo and running home strongly. Selections: STONE WRITER (1), TALK IS CHEAP (5), COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2), QUEENOFDANCE (8)

Another race where there looks to be some nice gate speed off the front row, with MAXX (1) looking to kick through and hold the front, where he should be suited over the mile. REPETITIVE (3) looks the one most likely to push the button when the green light comes on and has been racing consistently of late. JUST LIKA DREAM (2) has been racing well without winning and should find a nice position on speed with cover, giving her every chance to finish in the top three again here. CHEYS ANGEL (5) will be hoping for plenty of tempo throughout to allow her to rush home strongly, which she is capable of doing with the right run in transit. ROCKNALLOVERTHEWORLD (4) looks the best of the rest from his reasonable middle front-row draw. Selections: MAXX (1), JUST LIKA DREAM (2), CHEY'S ANGEL (5), REPETITIVE (3)

The final heat of the night, where although you would expect ALOT LIKE PENDLES (3) to go around at a very short price, I expect him to have to do a power of work sitting outside SHADES OF SILK (1), who possesses very good gate speed and should run them along at a very even tempo throughout. This should set it up for an enthralling finish for those watching the clock at the end of the race. It's hard to spot too many others capable of knocking off the favoured runners from their ideal draws, but ALWAYS AURORA (5) enjoys the mile distance and sitting off a hot speed, while MONTGOMERY BURNS (6) has been thereabouts of late and can't be left out of trifecta calculations. STEPUPANDANCE (2) will also be looking to run into the top three from her nice draw. Selections: ALOT LIKE PENDLES (3), SHADES OF SILK (1), ALWAYS AURORA (5), MONTGOMERY BURNS (6) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: Third heat of the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup here following two qualifiers at Melton last Friday as horses progress towards a $10,000 final back at HQ on November 20. Stacks of winning hopes, but ROBLEN RANGER (1) might be the best of them given his good gate speed, pole-marking draw and strong recent form. He led and hung on to win narrowly at Ballarat on October 29 in a slick enough last half of 56.9, which followed two handy runner-up placings at Cranbourne and Melton. He should run well. MONSIEUR FLAMEL (5) and ARE WESLEY (2) are the two Stephen Clarke-trained runners in the race, with the former heading here after a gutsy death-seat win at Kilmore and third placing in a previous heat of this series at Melton last time out. ARE WESLEY (2) has won his last two in slightly easier grade and must be respected, while KITSUNE (10) is perhaps a good runner at a price after a good first-up effort at long odds when fourth behind Cool Story in the first of the Bacchus Marsh Pacing Cup qualifiers last week. JUSJOHN (9), who gains a start as emergency, is an interesting runner and one I’ll be including in the Early Quaddie based off some nice enough efforts last campaign. SELECTIONS: ROBLEN RANGER (1), MONSIEUR FLAMEL (5), ARE WESLEY (2), KITSUNE (10)

OVERVIEW: This is the second heat of the Bacchus Marsh Trotters Cup and it looks a difficult race to sort out. LEANNE LEEANN (8) hasn’t won since all the way back in December of last year, but is knocking on the door for success. She draws for a pegs-line run, and from leader’s back or three back the fence, she’s a winning hope. Bob Kuchenmeister’s mare has been good her last four starts, including last time out at Maryborough when second to the handy Little Miss Valley while beating home three rivals here that reoppose. Happy to play her on the each-way if the price allows. NIGHT FLIGHT (7) is the speed influence from out wide on the front line and is probably the likely leader. He’s not overly strong late, but can certainly give them something to catch if he’s able to find the top. FLOATING MOUNTAIN (9) hasn’t been too far away of late but has had peg runs in those efforts and that might not eventuate here, while LOVE WHO (1) draws to lead or be leader’s back and can improve sharply on his latest effort when caught parked in the first heat of this series last Friday which saw JAKARTA (10) finish second and emergency APRIL SUN (4) place third. BACK: LEANNE LEEANN (8) – 1.5 units (each-way) SELECTIONS: LEANNE LEEANN (8), NIGHT FLIGHT (7), FLOATING MOUNTAIN (9), LOVE WHO (1)

OVERVIEW: HAPPILY (3) is a get-back, run-on type who needs luck in her races but is a very gifted pacer who often storms home and did just that when winning from last at Ballarat on October 29. It was a great effort and followed a close-up third placing to Jilliby Sniper – that horse has won twice since – when held up on the fence at Terang. I like her and she should be going close with even tempo and luck. RIVER STORM (4) had no chance from last in a fast last half at Melton in the IRT Graduate latest, but before that won well at Cranbourne and also did well when third to Cardigan Dan in a heat of the Vicbred Super Series back in August. Classy and a key danger. SECRET SERVICE AGENT (7) has a difficult gate to contend with but was a dominant winner two back before leading them up, absorbing pressure and boxing on okay into fifth in that hot IRT Graduate, while HOUSE PARTY (2) has been beaten as a short-priced favourite her last two in easier races than this, and while she is probably one I’m happy to overlook again, she must be regarded as a chance from the state’s powerhouse stable. ANGELS WATCHING (1) is the other key contender from the good gate and following a close-up second last time out at Kilmore. BACK: HAPPILY (3) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: HAPPILY (3), RIVER STORM (4), SECRET SERVICE AGENT (7), HOUSE PARTY (2)

OVERVIEW: SNACK LOVER (8) returns from a break in this 0-49 grade assignment following two trials at Terang. While thrashed by Golden Tribe on Tuesday night, he did a good job to finish in a bunch alongside Madrigal (14 wins) and Crime Writer (20 wins), which reads really well for a race like this. His maiden win was good at Ballarat back in April and he looks a progressive type in a contest where most are fairly well exposed. BLUE MIKI (7) slides back slightly in grade and was a winner of back-to-back races recently at Melton and Kilmore, FLIGHT LOUTENANT (5) did some nice work late despite being well beaten last Friday at Melton and is a contender, while ALPHA CRUCIS (2) and stablemates DOT BALL (3) and TEX GOES BANG (4) look the other winning hopes. BACK: SNACK LOVER (8) – 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: SNACK LOVER (8), BLUE MIKI (7), FLIGHT LOUTENANT (5), ALPHA CRUCIS (2)

OVERVIEW: SOMEONE SPECIAL (8) is a well-bred first starter by Always B Miki out of The Good Times, who has produced top pacers Very Pretty ($299,190) and Major Times ($314,755). She hails from the powerhouse Emma Stewart stable and heads to Geelong on the back of two solid trials at Melton and Terang. This isn’t a strong maiden, and she will be very short in the market. SEW HOPEFUL (7) is a 23-start maiden but has trialled up nicely at Melton following a couple of close-up efforts at Kilmore and Charlton, SONOFPLATINUM (5) just missed in a photo here at Geelong on October 16 and looks set to run a forward race in this company, while JILLIBY UTAH (4) has been thereabouts in recent efforts for Rory Coverdale and might be best of the rest. SELECTIONS: SOMEONE SPECIAL (8), SEW HOPEFUL (7), SONOFPLATINUM (5), JILLIBY UTAH (4)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY CLASSIC (5) hails from the state’s premier trotting barn of Marg and Paddy Lee and has shown some good promise in a few recent trials on the home track at Terang. He won one and wasn’t beaten far in the others, and looks to have some nice ability. Will lean his way. WHERDASUNDONTSHINE (2) is knocking on the door for a maiden success after back-to-back runner-up placings at Geelong and Maryborough and looks to have the best of the exposed form, quick beginner DANCE WITH ROXY (7) made a mistake when favourite last time out but did run two-straight runner-up placings in early October, while SYNTAX ERROR (1) draws well and has been running some honest races for Eddie Conroy of late. SELECTIONS: JILLIBY CLASSIC (5), WHERDASUNDONTSHINE (2), DANCE WITH ROXY (7), SYNTAX ERROR (1)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY CONNECTION (7) made a mistake on debut when favourite in the $75,000 Yabby Dam Farms 2YO Fillies Final and then made amends with a faultless display on Redwood Day at Maryborough when leading and charging clear in a nice last half to win by more than 20m. She looks above average and is the one to beat here in this clash for two-year-old trotters. ORLANDO VEYRON (5) settled three fence in the Redwood Classic and galloped late, but he ran okay before that for third behind megastar Verbici and did win a nice race early in the season, THE WOOL BROKER (4) broke through for his maiden triumph here at Geelong two starts ago before being outclassed in the Redwood, while PASTOR JAY JAY (1) draws well and did hit the line nicely late when third on debut at Kilmore on November 5. SELECTIONS: JILLIBY CONNECTION (7), ORLANDO VEYRON (5), THE WOOL BROKER (4), PASTOR JAY JAY (1) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R2 #8 LEANNE LEEANN – 1.5 units (each-way) R3 #3 HAPPILY – 3 units (win) R4 #8 SNACK LOVER – 4 units (win) EARLY QUADDIE 1,2,5,7,9,10/1,7,8,9/3,4,7/5,7,8 QUADDIE 5,7,8/8/2,5,7/7 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:DISTANT SUN (1) has been racing super without winning recently. She has been flashing home well late and gets a change of luck here with the better barrier. PARIS KAY (7) got it wrong with her manners last start, so we can forget that run. Her start prior was a second in the Swan Hill Trotters Cup, where she ran well chasing down the getaway winner. She is one of the classier horses in this race, but the barrier is tricky. LITTLE MISS MORGAN (9) is a smart mare who won well last start at Maryborough, flashing home from last. She beat DISTANT SUN (1) on that occasion, however, the barrier suits DISTANT SUN (1) here. ZARSKI (4) has a massive motor and a lot of ability, but his quirks bring risk. He galloped last start and can do things wrong. If he’s on his best behaviour, he’s one of, if not the most talented horses in this field. Also respecting WALLIS (2), who let down nicely for third last start. With some luck, he can be prominent here. BACK: DISTANT SUN (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: DISTANT SUN (1), PARIS KAY (7), LITTLE MISS MORGAN (9), ZARSKI (4)

OVERVIEW:ICANMOTOR (9) is a 20-time winner and finds a suitable race here, particularly with a maiden also in the field. He’s been out of the winner’s circle since finding a purple patch of form late last year. He sustained a three-wide run last start and still battled on well for fifth. He’s racing okay and barrier nine suits. FAKE CULLECTION (10) needs to overcome a wide back-row barrier, but she is racing okay. She was narrowly beaten at Kilmore last start after flashing home brilliantly. IMAGUNNARESTNGO (7) was in a race restricted to NR up to 45 last start and drops back to NR up to 38 here. It was an interesting run, as he seemed to be struggling to keep up with the horses in front of him at the bell, but then picked up the bit again late and let down okay. He’s not the fastest beginner, so he will likely drift back to the rear of the field and need some luck, but it’s a suitable race. OKTOLOVE (6) is one for the exotics if he gets some luck. If JOEYS HANGOVER (10), the emergency, gains a start, he’s a winning chance and would have likely been my top selection. SELECTIONS: ICANMOTOR (9), FAKE CULLECTION (10), IMAGUNNARESTNGO (7), OKTOLOVE (6)

OVERVIEW:TED BEAR (9) won impressively two starts ago at Melton, flashing around the field to win. Last start, he tired after leading. If he’s saved for one run here, he will be flashing home late. LORIMERMAJOR (2) was second behind the smart mare Harley Lane recently at Kilmore. He had barrier two on that occasion, settled midfield and flashed home impressively once he found clear running. He’s an experienced horse who can run well here with some luck. ANIMADO (1) was third last start after leading and tiring in the late stages. He can place again here from the barrier. CATIES SON (3) is third-up here and should be back to near peak fitness. Forget last start, when he hit the barrier arm and galloped, but still let down well late after catching the field. He is a smart horse at his best. BACK: TED BEAR (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: TED BEAR (9), LORIMERMAJOR (2), ANIMADO (1), CATIES SON (3)

OVERVIEW: This is an interesting race with many first starters. CATCH A BUTTERFLY (9) has all the ticks on paper to make her a nice filly. She is a full sister to Catch A Wave and a half-sister to Yambukian. She is trained by Emma Stewart and her trial form has been good, albeit in slow time. Looking forward to following this filly. ALWAYS BE VICKI (6) is a New Zealand-bred filly for Craig Demmler having her first career start. She has looked really good, winning her two Melton trials. In both trials, she was strong to the line but also under a grip, looking like she has a lot to offer. LIL SPARROW (3) is having her first career start for Kristy Butler. She won her recent trial at Shepparton and we will learn more about her here. FLYING JACKIE (2) has one career start. She got shuffled back at Shepparton and hit the line well for second. If she had been on the fence, her final quarter would have been 27.8. If she finds a good race map here, she could be flashing home again. Also respecting ASHANTE MAJOR (8), who is out of superstar broodmare For Dear Life, making him a half-brother to Pelosi. He’s bred to be a nice horse. SELECTIONS: CATCH A BUTTERFLY (9), ALWAYS BE VICKI (6), LIL SPARROW (3), FLYING JACKIE (2)

OVERVIEW:BUSLIN BRODY (9) has had some mixed form recently when it comes to his manners. He has been getting it wrong and galloping early. However, when he has been trotting throughout, he appears to be near career-best form. Hoping he can settle here from barrier nine, do everything right and be the one crossing the line first. I CHOOSE YOU (6) flashed home well from last to finish fourth last start at Maryborough. His class was on show recently against the top level of the three-year-old trotters when he finished second behind Munny The Munster in a Vicbred Super Series heat. He can get things wrong with his manners. RASTAMON (2) has good gate speed and will likely find the fence here. He performs best when he finds the fence and is racing well. PASS THE SALT (5) is a nice horse at his best. He was shuffled back last start at Maryborough but still let down well late. BACK: BUSLIN BRODY (9)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: BUSLIN BRODY (9), I CHOOSE YOU (6), RASTAMON (2), PASS THE SALT (5)

OVERVIEW:RAPTA (4) has a lot of ability when he trots throughout. Four starts ago, he ran an eye-catching second in a Need For Speed heat against a top-quality field. Since then, he has recorded another good placing and galloped twice. If he trots, he is the one to beat here. MOONSHINE LOUIE (2) has been racing well. He hasn’t been out of the top four in eight starts. He can make his own luck and should be able to map well here from barrier two. KYVALLEY REEVA (7) can get it wrong with her manners, but when she trots, she trots impressively. She galloped last start, but her two starts prior saw her trot throughout and win very well. If she trots, she can win. ALDEBARAN JAZMINE (5) has a strong last 800 metres on the clock at her best. If she gets a good trip, she can be flashing home late. BACK: RAPTA (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: RAPTA (4), MOONSHINE LOUIE (2), KYVALLEY REEVA (7), ALDEBARAN JAZMINE (5)

OVERVIEW:KIMCHI (5) is a reliable performer who is in good form. He let down nicely from midfield to win two starts ago at Kilmore. Last start, he was three-wide with cover for the last lap and sprinted well late for second. He has another sticky barrier, but he’s versatile enough to make his own luck. OUR MYSTERY BET (1) is a consistent performer who will get a good fence trip here. TASTE IT (7) sustained a good three-wide trip to win well last start. She is racing well, but her barrier makes it tricky here. HOME AND DRY (2) was unlucky last start, held up before running home nicely once he found clear air. He has a better barrier here and gets a chance for a change of luck. BACK: KIMCHI (5)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: KIMCHI (5), OUR MYSTERY BET (1), TASTE IT (7), HOME AND DRY (2)

OVERVIEW:WHIRILY MAURZ (1) is in career-best form, winning her last two starts very well. She has the best sectional times on paper and is full of confidence. She can win again. The biggest risk to her chances is her gate speed. The horses drawn to her outside, especially HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2), have better-known gate speed than her. She is a massive chance if she can hold a forward position. HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2) does look likely to find the fence here and, from there, can take advantage of a good trip. KNOW THE SCORE (3), at his best, is a winning chance in this field. There are a few question marks around some of his recent runs, but if he can map well here, he may find a chance to get back into form. THE HEATS ON LEXY (4) could map as the horse flashing home late if she gets some luck. ABRAHAM (8) is first up in 52 days and is having his first look at the Kilmore track. SELECTIONS: WHIRILY MAURZ (1), HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2), KNOW THE SCORE (3), THE HEATS ON LEXY (4)

OVERVIEW:FROSTY DROP (1) is a smart filly with great gate speed and general high speed. If she can stay close to the front, take advantage of her fence barrier and avoid having to work too hard, she’s a big winning chance here. BLACKINDEED (3) is fourth-up here and should be close to peak race fitness. She has finished third at her last two starts and let down well last start. If she can map well, she will be in the finish. RAKAROMPA (4) is a lightly raced mare who is second-up here. She let down nicely for second last start and I am expecting an improved performance with added fitness. TRYX VIXEN (5) is a smart filly who rarely runs a bad race, but she has a sticky barrier here. SELECTIONS: FROSTY DROP (1), BLACKINDEED (3), RAKAROMPA (4), TRYX VIXEN (5) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:SOLS ME NAME (4) is first up since tiring in the Vicbred Super Series Semi-Final in September. While it was a Group 1 series against the best horses in his age group, he did appear below his best in that performance. He was a good third in his heat the week prior. He is a classy horse at his best, remains lightly raced and has won two recent trials. BANJO STAR (2) is racing better than his numerical form suggests. He got too wide and too far back last start, making it difficult to make up ground. His previous effort was a smart fourth at Wagga in good time. MISTER HUNTER (9) is one of the best horses in this race on ability. He has 11 starts for six wins, including a Group 1 success in the APG Gold Bullion as a two-year-old in 2023. However, he hasn't raced since June 2024, and that was his only start since May 2023. He has had just two recent trials, making this a massive ask. First up after 865 days and now competing outside aged-group racing, he will need to be very sharp to win. DELIGHTFUL MIKI (1) is a smart, lightly raced mare who gets the ace barrier and the opportunity to use it to her advantage. Also strongly respecting ALOT LIKE JEANNIE (8), who has been racing at the top level among the three-year-old fillies this season. She won a Vicbred Super Series heat and possesses a brilliant turn of foot. She will need some luck from the barrier. BACK: SOLS ME NAME (4)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: SOLS ME NAME (4), BANJO STAR (2), MISTER HUNTER (9), DELIGHTFUL MIKI (1)

OVERVIEW: This race is full of progressive horses, making it a very competitive event. MASTER LOUEY (10) is a smart colt who rarely runs a bad race. He put together some really nice performances before winning well last start after leading at Ballarat. This assignment will be harder, as he is unlikely to find the front and will be racing over the short trip. However, he has the class to be competitive. STORM VENDETTA (6) contested the same race won by Master Louey last start but was too far back and wide to make up the ground. He defeated MASTER LOUEY (10) three starts ago at Ballarat, coming off his back to run past him. He has a great turn of foot, although the barrier makes things tricky. TOORAM DANNY (9) flashed home strongly at Echuca last start and was only narrowly defeated. He rarely runs a bad race and should get a good trip, following through early into the running line. SIR NIPPA (3) is first up back in Victoria following a campaign in Tasmania and could appreciate the change of scenery. HOLLOW LOG (4), METRO MEMORY (5), SAVANNAH BREEZE (7) and CHAINSMOKE (11) are all capable of featuring with the right luck in what looks a very even field. SELECTIONS: MASTER LOUEY (10), STORM VENDETTA (6), TOORAM DANNY (9), SIR NIPPA (3)

OVERVIEW:TALISKER SKIPPER (11) is in good form after winning well at Kilmore last start when leading. He will need to make his own luck from barrier 11 here, but his best sectional times are around two seconds quicker than the rest of this field. ARTY MCFLY (3) is a two-year-old having his fourth career start. He is first up here after finishing fifth in the $100,000 APG Final last start. This is his first attempt outside two-year-old racing. HALF PRICE BRIDE (9) was too wide and too far back to make up the ground at Echuca last start. She has been a little unlucky recently but finds an opportunity to turn her form around if she can map well. THE IRISHMAN (1) is a horse who isn't afraid to do some work in his races. He is racing well and gets the ace barrier, which he can use to his advantage. Also respecting CHEEZ (8), who is first up for new trainer Tasmyn Potter. SELECTIONS: TALISKER SKIPPER (11), ARTY MCFLY (3), HALF PRICE BRIDE (9), THE IRISHMAN (1),

OVERVIEW:DANCE FIGHTER (7) was a dominant winner at Maryborough last start when leading. It was a slowly run race, but she let down nicely and got the job done. She has been racing well and comes into this with winning confidence. This assignment will be tougher from the barrier. OLIVER SMUDGE (3) was eye-catching when returning with a win last start after three years on the sidelines. He galloped early, caught the field, made his move around them and was too good when letting down late. He will improve again with fitness, but his manners remain a big risk. SHINELIKETHESUN (5) is the best swooper in this field on the clock. If she is close enough, she is good enough, but she comes with some risk after galloping at her last four starts. ELARIA (1) is having her third career start. She finished third on debut at Maryborough, doing everything right and running safely to the line. She galloped last start, although it appeared she may have suffered some interference that caused her to break stride. She recovered and ran on reasonably well. She should produce an improved performance here with added fitness. SELECTIONS: DANCE FIGHTER (7), OLIVER SMUDGE (3), SHINELIKETHESUN (5), ELARIA (1)

OVERVIEW:WIND STORM (8) was an impressive first-up winner at Maryborough last start, racing away to score by 21.9 metres. She has the best sectional times in this field, but will need to overcome the tricky barrier eight. FRANKS ALOT (2) is an interesting trotter. He raced in the breeze to finish a good second on debut, then followed that up with a dominant win at Maryborough before getting it wrong with his manners last start. If he can trot throughout and get forward, he will be a big threat. BIRMINGHAM GIRL (1) was good on debut when finishing third but got it wrong with her manners at Kilmore last start. She will need to trot throughout here. BIG RAIN (5) is a well-mannered trotter who is always competitive. With the right run and some luck, she can capitalise. BACK: WIND STORM (8) –2 units (win) SELECTIONS: WIND STORM (8), FRANKS ALOT (2), BIRMINGHAM GIRL (1), BIG RAIN (5)

OVERVIEW:BUILDTHEMANASTATUE (1) returns from a short campaign in Tasmania. He had a tough run but still finished fifth in the $75,000 Dandy Patch Final at Hobart last start after winning his heat. He is a classy runner, but faces the challenge of being a two-year-old competing against older horses. Barrier one certainly suits. BEAU BECA (2) led and battled on well for second at Kilmore last start. He is racing okay and should map well here. ARTIST (6) has been racing reasonably well, although he can be a little inconsistent. He finished fifth last start after racing in the breeze. Barrier six makes things tricky, but at his best he is a winning chance. BONA KHAN (3) is a fast horse who can be effective whether saved for one run or using his gate speed. If he gets some luck here, he cannot be forgotten. BACK: BUILDTHEMANASTATUE (1)– 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BUILDTHEMANASTATUE (1), BEAU BECA (2), ARTIST (6), BONA KHAN (3)

OVERVIEW: This looks a very even maiden with plenty of chances. Any horse in this field could win, and it wouldn't come as a surprise. EVA EXPRESS (7) has been racing okay. She led and took a sit at Kilmore last start before running home well to be beaten by a neck. She faces a more challenging barrier here, but should continue to improve, with this being just her fifth career start. SPOT THE DEVIL (1) flashed home nicely to finish third in the same race last start. He gets a change of luck here with barrier one, a draw he has had only once previously in his 48 career starts. ITS JUST RUBY (2) looked physically outstanding at Kilmore last start. I was on track before the race and she really caught my eye. She also performed better than the market suggested. She was shuffled back to last but ran home well, and gets a much better barrier here. She has the gate speed to make use of the draw and could be an improver in this event. DYGANALI (6) has been racing okay and looks ready to break through for his maiden victory. Barrier six is the main challenge. BACK: ITS JUST RUBY (2)– 1 unit (win)/ 2 units (place) SELECTIONS: EVA EXPRESS (7), SPOT THE DEVIL (1), ITS JUST RUBY (2), DYGANALI (6)

OVERVIEW:UNCLE TREV (6) has been racing regularly at Shepparton and Wagga recently and gets his first look at Melton here. He is a smart horse who rarely runs a bad race and has the best sectional times in this event. The barrier makes things difficult, but his class should shine through. SPRINGFIELD RIVER (5) is a progressive pacer who I believe we haven't seen the best of yet. He was a good second last start in a tough race, chasing runaway leaders and letting down nicely. The barrier is awkward here, but he is racing well. SPEEDY HEALEY (3) rarely runs a bad race and is always capable of letting down nicely when he gets a good trip. THEROUX (2) was inconvenienced last start when dragged back, but still managed to let down reasonably well. He is racing well and should map positively here. DIGBY JOY (7) looks likely to get the perfect run through in this race behind the likely leader in the race EBONY BELLE (1). She was running on nicely late last time out into second behind Erasmus. She should be able to press forward in this race and looks the one to beat despite the draw. He was forced to race without cover last time out and just faded late but may just be better suited driven quietly in his races. CALL IT BLING (5) draws a touch awkwardly in this race but does look to be a standout on class. He got back last time out and couldn’t get into the race late which was taken out in good time by Jaccka Cooper. SELECTIONS: CALL IT BLING (5), HIGHNMIGHTY (3), MACK ATTACK (4), SURPRISE BABY (2) SUGGESTED BET: CALL IT BLING (5) to win.

BROADWAYBEAUTY (4) smashed the clock in a recent trial rating 1.53.4 winning by a big margin there. If she goes anywhere near repeating that effort in this race it’ll be times and margins.
